description: nf-core/cutandrun samplesheet context. One row per paired-end library: its group (the target), replicate number and the IgG control group it is normalised against.

peakcaller.help: Peak caller(s). SEACR is the default and suits CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag's low background; with two, the first is the primary caller: only its peaks get the consensus, the FRiP score and the peak count.

normalisation_mode.help: Signal normalisation. Spikein scales each library by its reads on the spike-in genome (E. coli carry-over DNA by default); use CPM when the libraries have no spike-in or too few spike-in reads.

spikein_genome.help: iGenomes key of the spike-in genome: K12-MG1655 (E. coli, the carry-over of pA-MNase/pAG-Tn5 preps), R64-1-1 (yeast) or BDGP6 (fruit fly). Read only with normalisation_mode Spikein.

use_control.help: Normalise peak calls against an IgG control group named in the control column. Set false when the samplesheet names no control.

igg_scale_factor.help: Scale applied to the IgG control before it is used to normalise peaks.

seacr_peak_threshold.help: SEACR returns the top fraction (0 to 1) of peaks by total signal when no control is used.

seacr_norm.help: SEACR normalisation: 'non' when the signal is already spike-in normalised, 'norm' otherwise.

macs2_narrow_peak.help: MACS2 narrow-peak mode; false calls broad peaks (histone marks such as H3K27me3). Read only when macs2 is a peak caller.

dedup_target_reads.help: Remove duplicates from target libraries too (controls are always deduplicated). Usually left off for CUT&RUN, where identical fragments are expected at strong sites.

remove_mitochondrial_reads.help: Drop mitochondrial reads before peak calling.

end_to_end.help: Bowtie2 end-to-end mode; false uses local mode.

minimum_alignment_q_score.help: Drop alignments below this mapping quality.

consensus_peak_mode.help: Consensus peaks per group (default) or one set over every target sample.

replicate_threshold.help: Minimum number of replicates a consensus peak must appear in.

pipeline.name: nf-core/cutandrun
pipeline.core_rule: Required columns, in this order and no others: group, replicate, fastq_1, fastq_2, control. Paired-end only. Rows of one target share a group and number their replicates from 1; the IgG control libraries are their own group, with an empty control, and every target row names that group in control.

validation_rules: group is identical for the replicates of one target (no spaces); replicate is an integer from 1 within each group. A library sequenced over several runs keeps the same group and replicate, and the pipeline merges its runs.
Paired-end only: every row needs both fastq_1 and fastq_2, gzipped FASTQ ending in .fastq.gz or .fq.gz. A single-end cohort cannot run cutandrun.

control names the group of the IgG (or other background) control libraries, never the row's own group; a control row's own control is empty. Controls with as many replicates as a target are paired replicate by replicate, otherwise replicate 1 of the control serves every replicate.
With use_control true (the default) at least one row must name a control; with no control libraries set use_control false.
The samplesheet has no antibody column: name each group after its target (h3k27me3, ctcf), as the antibody is recorded nowhere else in the run.

population_priority: Group the libraries by target from NExtSEEK metadata (antibody, target, condition); IgG or no-antibody libraries form the control group.
Use accession_rows for fastq columns; ask the user which group is the control when the metadata does not say.
